claims.claim: The page is explicitly scoped to archived CUDA 13.0.2 PTX ISA 9.0 and correctly warns that representative forms still require typed operands, valid descriptors, collective participation, lifetimes, completion, and target/toolchain support.

evidence.locator: instruction grammar, target ISA notes, and tcgen05 memory-consistency model
evidence.observation: The archive versions grammar/targets and places the listed operand, participation, lifetime, and completion conditions on these instruction families.

challenge.alternative: The snippets are complete inline-assembly functions or rolling PTX semantics can be substituted without a version check.
challenge.check: Inspect operand declarations and target/version notes required by the archived grammar.
challenge.outcome: The forms omit surrounding declarations by design, and support is explicitly versioned; the scope warning is necessary and accurate.

claims.claim: The representative alloc/load-address/MMA/commit/dealloc forms and prose accurately describe a cta_group::1 unscaled F16 path: alloc writes a 32-bit taddr to shared memory and counts columns, allocation/deallocation are warp-collective, MMA D is in TMEM, commit attaches prior completion to an mbarrier, every allocation is freed, and one kernel uses one CTA-group mode.

evidence.locator: alloc/dealloc grammar, issue granularity, and lifecycle
evidence.observation: The exact forms, shared result, column unit, warp collectivity, and required deallocation match.

evidence.locator: unscaled floating-point grammar, CTA-group rule, and D semantics
evidence.observation: The five-operand f16 form, TMEM D, group modes, and same-group-per-kernel restriction match.
Commit tracks completion of prior asynchronous tcgen05 work with the displayed barrier form.

challenge.alternative: Alloc returns a column index directly in a register, ncols counts rows, MMA requires a lane-disable vector, or commit waits synchronously.
challenge.check: Compare the exact unscaled grammar and optional operands with the alloc destination and commit description.
challenge.outcome: Alloc stores a b32 taddr in shared memory and counts columns; the five-operand MMA is valid without the optional lane-disable vector; commit signals completion asynchronously.

claims.claim: The displayed 32x32b.x1 ld/st and 128x256b cp forms are legal; ld/st are asynchronous warp-collective TMEM-register transfers with their matching waits, cp moves SMEM to TMEM, and cp/MMA source/destination lifetimes extend through their documented completion.

evidence.locator: ld/st grammar, repetition table, collectivity, and wait
evidence.observation: 32x32b.x1 uses one register per thread, ld/st are warp-collective and asynchronous, and wait::ld/st provide completion.

evidence.locator: cp grammar, 128x256b example, and asynchronous semantics
evidence.observation: The exact cta_group::1 copy is shared-memory descriptor to TMEM and participates in tcgen05 completion/lifetime rules.

challenge.alternative: x1 is invalid, the waits are generic barriers, or cp copies TMEM to shared memory.
challenge.check: Use the shape/repetition table, wait grammar, and cp operand direction.
challenge.outcome: x1 is listed, waits target prior ld/st from the executing thread, and cp's destination is taddr while its source is sdesc.

claims.claim: The four completion/ordering bullets correctly distinguish TMA mbarrier byte completion, tcgen05 commit completion, ld/st waits, and before/after_thread_sync cross-thread tcgen ordering; the fences are not completion substitutes.

evidence.observation: TMA load completion decrements byte transaction count on its barrier.
Commit attaches prior MMA/cp/shift completion to an mbarrier.
The fences constrain tcgen05 issue around execution ordering and do not wait for async completion.

challenge.alternative: One CTA barrier or after_thread_sync can replace every listed mechanism.
challenge.check: Match each producer/consumer edge to the normative instruction that completes or orders it.
challenge.outcome: The ISA assigns distinct state and scope to each edge, so none is a universal substitute.

claims.claim: The packed conversion and typed move forms have the stated one-byte E2M1x2 source, 32-bit F16x2 result, and b32-to-four-b8 decomposition semantics, while PTX makes no universal speed promise.

evidence.observation: The E2M1x2/F16x2 types and widths match.
Four byte destinations can receive a b32 source when declarations match; no performance comparison is specified.

challenge.alternative: The input is a 32-bit scalar FP4, mov changes numeric representation, or the ISA guarantees lower latency.
challenge.check: Apply packed type widths and mov's bitwise typed-copy semantics.
challenge.outcome: The input is one packed byte, mov preserves bits across equal total width, and the documentation contains no timing theorem.

claims.claim: The three ld.global forms are legal 16/32-byte vector loads; no_allocate and evict_last are nonbinding L1 eviction-priority hints, so the page correctly rejects guaranteed bypass/residency and scopes performance to the exact access pattern.

evidence.locator: ld grammar, vector examples, and cache operators
evidence.observation: The forms and widths match; eviction-priority qualifiers are performance hints that may not be respected.

challenge.alternative: The qualifier names prescribe deterministic cache behavior or v4.u64 is four bytes.
challenge.check: Read the cache-hint caveat and multiply vector arity by the 64-bit element width.
challenge.outcome: The behavior is advisory, and v4.u64 is 256 bits (32 bytes).

claims.claim: The CLC fragment and prose accurately show an asynchronous 16-byte shared response completed on an mbarrier, followed by success and first-CTA-coordinate queries; the request cancels a not-yet-launched unit and takes no desired tile ID.

evidence.locator: try_cancel grammar, response, completion, and query_cancel sections
evidence.observation: The displayed request/query forms, 16-byte response, wait-before-query requirement, cancellation target, and no-coordinate request semantics match.

challenge.alternative: try_cancel returns coordinates directly or accepts the work ID to steal.
challenge.check: Inspect request operands separately from query_cancel output operands.
challenge.outcome: The request has only response and barrier addresses; coordinates are decoded from a completed successful response.

claims.claim: The two TMA forms are valid 2D global-to-cluster-shared tile loads; multicast uses .multicast::cluster plus a 16-bit mask and sends data and barrier completion to corresponding offsets in selected live destination CTAs.

evidence.observation: Both exact forms, tensor-map coordinates, mbarrier, qualifier, mask width, corresponding offsets, and destination lifetime requirements match.

challenge.alternative: The shorter .multicast spelling is legal, the barrier is signaled only in the issuer, or destination CTAs need not be resident.
challenge.check: Inspect the qualifier set and multicast destination/completion description.
challenge.outcome: Only .multicast::cluster is legal, completion is multicast to matching offsets, and remote shared memory must remain live.
